note: BUG#28 (QualityControl ledger) — a creating command whose `given` fails while its identity already exists refused `AlreadyExists` in Rust and `GivenNotMet` in Ruby: `CommandInterpreter#hydrate_complete_state`, for a `complete_state? && state_independent?` command (`Member.Join`'s own `given` dereferences a fresh `sponsor` argument, never the aggregate's own not-yet-existing state), defers its `AlreadyExists` check all the way to `step_save` — AFTER `enforce_givens` already ran — while unmodified Rust's `Hydrate::Create` checked `repo.find` eagerly, before any given, unconditionally. Confirmed genuinely broken before this fixture existed: `s1` enrolls, `m1` joins under `s1` while it's in good standing (succeeds), `s1` is suspended, then `m1` joins AGAIN under the now-suspended `s1` — a genuine duplicate identity AND a failing given on the SAME dispatch. Ruby answers `Join refused — the sponsor is in good standing` (GivenNotMet); unmodified Rust answered `Join creates a Member that already exists — handle.value "m1"` (AlreadyExists) instead.
